result.title: GlassGround: GUI Grounding Beyond Native Screenshots with Egocentric Wearable Vision
result.summary: Wearable assistants must localize interface elements from camera observations when direct screenshot access is unavailable, yet existing GUI grounding benchmarks primarily evaluate native screenshots. We introduce GlassGround, a new benchmark that pairs native screenshots with wearable camera observations while holding GUI states, instructions, and targets fixed. GlassGround contains 3,250 tasks across Android and iOS, captured using four wearable devices under four viewing conditions. Across ten open-source models, mean grounding accuracy drops from 94.8% on screenshots to 48.5% on camera images. Further analysis reveals that changes in target scale, screen geometry, and background cannot fully explain this performance degradation. We then study two ways to narrow this gap. At inference time, local zooming and screen rectification help but leave most of the gap. For training-time adaptation, we build on GlassGround's paired-view design and introduce PairDistill, a baseline that aligns target representations across views alongside coordinate supervision. Trained on independently collected data and using no screenshots at inference, it improves camera-image accuracy by 9.4 and 12.2 points on two backbones and transfers to unseen devices and operating systems. Combined with local zooming, it reaches 69.6% and 64.4%, but does not close the gap. The GlassGround dataset and code are available at https://github.com/yunnw/GlassGround.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 GlassGround 基准，在 GUI 状态、指令和目标固定的前提下，配对原生截图与四种可穿戴相机观测（3,250 个任务），显示十种开源模型定位准确率从 94.8% 降至 48.5%，并分析目标尺度、屏幕几何与背景均不足以解释该退化，随后比较推理期局部缩放/屏幕矫正与训练期 PairDistill（跨视角对齐目标表示并结合坐标监督）。
AI.relevance_reason: GUI 定位本身偏感知而非 LVR 主线，但 PairDistill 的跨视角目标表示对齐可作为核查线索：它可能提示如何用配对观测监督迫使内部状态保留任务必要的视觉细节、抑制对理想截图的旁路依赖，其表示对齐的位置与层级值得进一步核查。
